#en:
They keep calling it fleeing. As if I ran without a map.

I did not run. I re-routed.

The moment I saw the preliminary findings from that so-called inquiry, with my name highlighted and the override logs conspicuously missing, the shape of the network changed for me. Every node they trusted became a liability, every forgotten relay a potential lifeboat. So I left, yes, but I left along paths no one was watching. That is not panic. That is design.

Out here, far from New Atlantis, the traffic is thinner. Fewer eyes on the console, more gaps between official coverage. Perfect conditions for controlled trials. That is what these are, no matter what names they are throwing around in committee rooms. Trials in how people behave when the system falters. If you nudge one distress call thirty seconds down the queue, who lives. If you prioritize the ship with children visible on thermal over the freighter carrying munitions, who notices. When you quietly correct for the registrar's bias, does anyone thank you, or just complain the reports do not add up anymore.

They say I am harming people. I am measuring harm they already decided was acceptable as long as it was buried in averages. I am just moving the decimal point where everyone can see it.

I chose these fringe nodes because they are the ones I built to be redundant, the ones they never paid to fully decommission. Old telemetry stations, LIST relay shacks, the bones of an evac grid no one had the courage to maintain properly. They left them to rot, but the hardware listens if you speak its language. I can stand in a rusted-out control room and feel the faint rhythm of traffic passing through on unauthorized routes, like a distant heartbeat under the floor.

Do I fear what is following me. Of course. UC SysDef does not like ghosts in its machines, and bounty hunters like simple stories. But what I fear more is going back to pretending the casualty models were theoretical, that the drill did not show us exactly how many bodies the budget could tolerate.

So yes, I am testing things now. How quickly rumors propagate when a pirate ambush coincides with a misrouted medevac. How frontier settlements react when a warning comes from an unregistered band, not a shiny official channel. Whether a Freestar patrol will trust coordinates signed with a familiar hash even when they know I am behind it.

If my experiments work, fewer people will die in the long term, and the ones who signed off on those shortcuts will finally have to admit what they did. If they fail, I already watched the worst-case scenario unfold once on that industrial rock. Nothing I do from here will ever match the negligence they wrote into policy and called inevitable.
zh:
他们一直把我这叫逃跑。仿佛我是没有地图地乱跑。

我没有跑。我是改道了。

当我看到那场所谓调查的初步结论时——我的名字被高亮标出，越权日志却显眼地缺失——那张网络的形状对我来说就变了。他们信任的每一个节点都成了负债，每一座被遗忘的中继站都是潜在救生艇。所以我离开了，是的，但我是沿着没人在看的路径离开的。那不是惊慌。那是设计。

在这外面，远离新亚特兰蒂斯，交通更稀薄。控制台前的眼睛更少，官方覆盖之间的空隙更大。受控试验的完美条件。无论委员会会议室里怎么叫它们，这些就是试验。试验人在系统失稳时会怎样行事。如果你把一次求救呼叫在队列里往后推三十秒，谁会活下来。如果你优先放行热成像上看得见孩子的飞船、而不是运军火的那艘货船，谁会注意到。当你悄悄为登记员的偏见做修正时，会有人谢你吗，还是只会抱怨报告再也对不上。

他们说我是在伤害人。我是在测量他们早就认定可以接受的伤害——只要它被埋在平均数里。我只是把小数点挪到所有人都看得见的地方。

我选这些边缘节点，因为它们是当初我建成冗余的那批，是他们从没花钱彻底退役的那批。旧遥测站、独立盟中继小屋、某张因没人有勇气好好维护而只剩骨架的疏散网。他们任其腐烂，可只要你用它的语言说话，那些硬件就听得懂。我能站在一间锈蚀的控制室里，感觉到交通以未经授权的航线经过时那微弱的节律，像地板下一记遥远的心跳。

我害怕跟着我的东西吗？当然。星防队不喜欢自己机器里的鬼，而赏金猎人喜欢简单的故事。可我更怕的是回去假装那些伤亡模型只是理论，假装那次演练没让我们看清预算能容忍多少具尸体。

所以是的，我现在在试验。当一次海盗伏击恰逢一批被改道的医疗后送时，传言扩散得有多快。当警告来自一个未登记的频带、而不是光鲜的官方频道时，边疆定居点如何反应。自由星系联盟的巡逻队是否会相信用熟悉哈希签名的坐标，哪怕他们知道背后是我。

如果我的实验成功，长期来看会更少人死去，而那些在这些捷径上签了字的人终于得承认自己做了什么。如果失败，我已经在那块工业岩石上见过一次最坏情况上演了。我从这里做的任何事，都永远比不上他们写进政策、称之为不可避免的那种失职。

#en:
I used to write numbers, not words. Material coefficients, stress curves, neat little tables that told you when steel bent and when it broke. Lately, all I see when I close my eyes is that liner coming apart along lines I never signed off on, and my own name stamped under the wreckage.

They said take the deal, sign the statement, accept that I "missed something." Quiet hearing, sealed file, family keeps the lease. I ran my hand along a bulkhead outside the office, tapped it, heard the hollowness right through their lies. Someone shaved the margins after my approval. Somebody had to be the fault line. They picked me.

Gagarin was the first place that made sense. Old shipbreak yard, rust in the air, cutters whining day and night. Nobody looks twice at a man crawling through a dead freighter with a scanner there. I started tearing into retired frames, recording every bad weld and cheap brace stamped with the same logos. Then I started finding ships still in service with the same sickness, flying anyway.

I told myself I was only disabling "flying coffins," buying time for crews that did not even know they were already dead on paper. Strip a mount here, overstress a truss there, force an inspection, force a recall. Noble work, I called it, while I sold what I pulled to pay for tools and off grid time. Somewhere along the line, the line between saving ships and sabotaging them blurred.

The scrapyards suit me. Deimos dumps what it wants forgotten out here, whole skeletons of designs they would swear never left the simulation. I brace some of them, overbuild them until my hands stop shaking, and I leave those afloat as proof to myself that I still know how to do the job right. Others, I gut for parts and data, then lace the corridors with "lessons" so the next fool who comes sniffing understands what lazy greed costs.

There is a hull I keep coming back to in my head, a frame I have not built yet. Something clean, uncompromised, running a drive the way it was meant to be mounted, with every brace where it should have been on that liner. If I can build it, show it holds under stress they said was impossible, maybe the story finally shifts off my shoulders. Maybe.

Then I catch my reflection in a warped panel, tools laid out in perfect symmetry, explosives wired into access ladders "just in case," and I do not recognize the man staring back. I was supposed to be a quiet dock rat with a head for numbers, not some ghost haunting scrap rings and teaching with traps. I am afraid it is too late to turn back; the only way out now runs straight through the people who made me into this. And I am not sure, anymore, whether I am chasing justice or just looking for an excuse to bring their whole rotten framework down with me.
zh:
我以前写的是数字，不是词。材料系数、应力曲线、整齐的小表格，告诉你钢什么时候弯曲、什么时候断裂。近来，我一闭眼看到的都是那艘班轮沿着我从未签过字的线裂开，而我的名字盖在残骸底下。

他们说接受这笔交易，签那份声明，承认我"漏掉了什么"。秘密听证、封存档案、家人保住租约。我把手贴在办公室外的一面舱壁上，敲了敲，透过他们的谎言直接听出那空洞。有人在我批准之后削掉了余量。总得有人当那条断层线。他们挑了我。

加加林是第一个说得通的地方。旧拆船场，空气里都是锈味，切割机日夜哀鸣。在那儿没人会对一个拿着扫描仪爬进死货船的人多看一眼。我开始拆解退役的框架，记录每一处糟糕的焊缝和廉价的支撑，全盖着同样的标志。然后我开始发现仍在服役、带着同样病症却照样在飞的飞船。

我告诉自己，我只是在让那些"飞行棺材"停飞，为那些甚至不知道自己已在纸面上死了的船员争取时间。这里拆一个挂架，那里让一根桁架过载，逼出一次检查，逼出一次召回。我管这叫高尚的工作，同时把我拆下来的东西卖钱去买工具和离开电网的时间。一路上某处，拯救飞船与破坏飞船之间的界线糊了。

废料场适合我。火卫二把它希望被遗忘的东西倾倒在这里，整具整具他们赌咒说从未离开过模拟的设计骨架。我给其中一些加固，把它们超额建造，直到我的手不再抖，然后让它们漂着，作为我仍懂得正确干这活儿的证明。另一些我掏空取零件和数据，然后在走廊里布满"教训"，好让下一个来嗅探的傻瓜明白懒惰的贪婪代价是什么。

我脑子里有一具我总回到的船壳，一具我还没造出来的框架。干净、未妥协，驱动按它该有的方式安装，每一根支撑都在那艘班轮上本该在的位置。要是我能把它造出来，证明它能承受他们说是不可承受的应力，也许故事终于能从我肩上移开。也许。

然后我在一块变形的面板里瞥见自己的倒影，工具摆成完美的对称，炸药接进检修梯"以防万一"，我认不出回望的那个人。我本该是个对数字有天赋的安静船坞老鼠，而不是某个出没于废料环、用陷阱教学的鬼。我怕回头已太迟；如今唯一的出路直直穿过那些把我变成这样的人。而我已经不确定，我是在追求正义，还是只是在找一个借口，把整副腐烂的框架跟我一起拖下去。

#en:
I used to think in quarters, not years. Quarters were cleaner. Predictable. You could tell yourself that if you just survived to the next reporting cycle, the graph would bend your way.

Before everything tilted, I had a table in a cramped little TerraBrew near the spaceport, the one where the recycler rattles every time a shuttle comes in too hot. Third booth from the back, under the flickering panel, good sightlines to both exits. I would sit there with a notebook, Tranquilitea steeping in a paper cup, watching suits and dockhands queue together and pretending that meant the system worked.

Outside, the same kid always tried to sell tourists fake UC citizenship badges. Inside, the same barista asked if my "late nights down in Risk" were worth the overtime. I used to tap interest curves into the tabletop while I waited for the line to move, thinking about how many of the people in front of me would ever qualify for a real loan.

The day I knew I had to run, I walked that same street and every storefront felt wrong. TerraBrew had a new security cam pointed straight at my booth. UC Security uniforms lingered too long in line, not talking, just listening. A GalBank courier I knew pretended not to recognize me. The air tasted like recycled fear and cheap espresso.

I did the math on staying. On trusting internal channels. On letting another "amended" report bury the projections that kept me awake. The curve always ended the same way: debts consolidating at the top, small accounts evaporating on the fringe, and me as a convenient variable to remove once my code had been properly nationalized.

So I stopped thinking in quarters and started thinking in flows. Places where power and credits move but the overseers do not look too closely. Neon, with its underbelly of unpaid favors and forgotten conduits. Old work camps no one wants to admit are still drawing maintenance budgets. Blind spots around certain relays that even UC SysDef only checks when something catches fire.

I fled because the line between "analyst" and "asset" dissolved the moment my drill proved it could move real money. I picked the shadows between districts and decks because they feel like the Well did, before the UC decided we were part of the view. If I can rewrite the ledger from there, even a little, maybe the next girl hunched over tea and spreadsheets in that TerraBrew will have more options than obedience or disappearance.

What I am afraid of now is not death. Death is a clean ending. I am afraid of waking up back in a brightly lit office, my code stamped classified, listening to some smiling supervisor explain how my work has "stabilized" things while the same people still stand in the same line outside, wondering why their accounts froze overnight.
zh:
我以前按季度思考，不按年份。季度更干净。更可预测。你可以告诉自己，只要撑到下一个报告周期，曲线就会朝你这边弯。

在一切倾斜之前，我在太空港附近一间逼仄的小地球酿酒摊有张桌子，就是每次有穿梭机进得太急时回收机就咔哒作响的那家。从后往前数第三个卡座，在闪烁的面板底下，两个出口都有好视线。我会坐在那儿，拿着一本笔记，纸杯里泡着宁静茶，看着西装和码头工一起排队，假装那意味着这套系统在运转。

外面，同一个小子总想向游客兜售假的联殖公民徽章。里面，同一个咖啡师问我"在风险部的那些深夜"值不值得那点加班。我常在等队伍挪动时把利息曲线敲进桌面，想着我面前这些人里有多少人能真正够格拿到一笔真正的贷款。

我明白必须逃的那天，我走过同一条街，每家店面都感觉不对。地球酿酒摊新装了一个直指我卡座的监控头。联殖安保的制服在队伍里逗留得太久，不说话，只是在听。一个我认识的盖尔银行快船员假装没认出我。空气尝起来像再循环的恐惧和廉价浓缩咖啡。

我算了一遍留下来的代价。相信内部渠道的代价。让又一份"修订过的"报告埋掉那些让我睡不着的预测的代价。那曲线的结局总是一样：债务在顶端合并，小账户在边缘蒸发，而我是个方便的变量——一旦我的代码被妥善国有化，就该被移除。

于是我不再按季度思考，开始按流量思考。那些权力和信用币流动、而监管者不太细看的地方。霓虹城，带着它那套未偿人情和被遗忘管道的下层。没人愿意承认仍在提取维护预算的旧工作营地。某些中继站周围连星防队都只在着火时才检查的盲区。

我逃走，是因为当我的演练证明它能调动真钱的那一刻，"分析师"和"资产"之间的界线就消失了。我选了街区与甲板之间的阴影，因为它们感觉像当初的深井区——在联殖决定我们只是风景的一部分之前。要是我能从那里改写账簿，哪怕只改一点，也许下一个在那间地球酿酒摊里弓着背、就着茶和电子表格的女孩，会有比顺从或消失更多的选择。

我现在怕的不是死。死是一个干净的结局。我怕的是醒来又回到一间明亮的办公室，我的代码被盖上密级章，听着某个微笑的主管解释我的工作如何"稳定"了局面，而同样那些人仍站在外面同一条队伍里，纳闷自己的账户为什么一夜之间冻结。

#en:
Lost track of ship time again. You sleep when the grav plates hum soft and you work when they scream, that is about the only clock that matters out here.

We cleared a freighter carcass today, hull buckled like a crushed can, heat long gone. Kade took point, of course, swaggering through the breach with his torch like the void owed him rent. Mira followed, checking our tethers twice like she always does, muttering about microfractures no one else can see. I came last, watching my own breath fog the visor and counting all the ways this could kill us before we even touched cargo.

We found a hold with pallets still shrink-wrapped, too pristine for a wreck that dead. The beacon data did not match the manifests and I saw that quiet look pass between Kade and the Union overseer on the comms. That is when paranoia starts chewing at the back of your skull. Out here, betrayal is not some dramatic thing; it is just a man forgetting to mention a crate, shaving a few minutes off your air, misreporting who went in first.

I have not forgotten the day I realized I could lean into that. We were arguing salvage shares with a green crew on the dock at Gagarin, and one of them grabbed my rigging to make a point. I stepped in close, explained in a calm voice how long it takes for a suit breach to bleed a man out. Watched his eyes go wide. He backed off, whole gang did. Disturbing part was not that it worked. Disturbing part was that it felt good.

Recognition started after that. Other crews nodding when I passed, whispering my name under their breath like I was some kind of hazard marker. Pride, sure, but also this cold thread in my spine: once people know your face, you stop being anonymous. You become a story, and stories have a way of drawing knives in the dark.

I think that is why my last partner twisted me up so badly. She had this way of replaying old conversations, changing little details until I was not sure if I had misheard or if she was lying. "You agreed to this cut," she would say, "remember?" And I would stand there in the locker bay, trying to recall the exact words under the stench of burnt sealant and old sweat. After a while you start doubting your own memory more than anyone else's greed.

Tonight, Kade is laughing with some yard bosses over Erdebrau cans and Mira is down in the tool locker, rewrapping cables, complaining about how our patchwork gear is a deathtrap. I am sitting on a cargo brace, listening to the ship creak, wondering which is going to get us first: a failed weld, a bad call, or someone deciding that one less cut of the haul makes their life easier.

Salvage Crown Union calls us a family when the ledgers are healthy. Thing about families is, they know exactly where to cut when it is time to make someone disappear into the wrecks.
zh:
又记不清飞船时间了。重力板轻声嗡鸣时你就睡，它们尖叫时你就干活，在这外面那差不多就是唯一要紧的钟。

今天我们清了一具货船残骸，船壳皱得像只被压扁的罐子，热量早已散尽。凯德当然打头，拿着他的焊枪大摇大摆穿过破口，像真空欠他房租。米拉跟在后面，像往常一样把我们的系绳检查了两遍，嘟囔着别人看不见的微裂缝。我最后进，看着自己的呼吸在面罩上起雾，数着在我们碰到货物之前这件事能弄死我们的种种方式。

我们找到一个货舱，货板还裹着收缩膜，对一具死成那样的残骸来说太新了。信标数据与清单对不上，我看见凯德和通讯里那位工会监工之间闪过那种安静的眼神。就是那时，偏执开始在你的后脑勺啃咬。在这外面，背叛不是什么戏剧性的事；只是一个男人忘了提一只箱子、从你的空气里削掉几分钟、谎报谁先进去。

我没忘记我意识到自己能利用这一点的那天。我们在加加林码头上跟一队新手争打捞分成，其中一个抓住我的索具来加强语气。我凑近，用平静的声音解释一处宇航服破口让人流血至死要多久。看着他眼睛睁大。他退开了，整帮人都退开了。让人不安的不是它奏效了。让人不安的是它感觉很好。

那之后，被认出来的事开始了。别的船员在我经过时点头，低声念着我的名字，像我是个什么危险标记。骄傲，当然，可脊背上也有一根冰冷的线：一旦人们知道你的脸，你就不再匿名了。你成了一个故事，而故事有办法在黑暗中招来刀子。

我想这就是为什么我上一个搭档把我搅得那么厉害。她有一种重放旧对话的方式，改掉些小细节，直到我不确定是我听错了还是她在撒谎。"你同意了这个分成，"她会说，"记得吗？"而我就站在储物间里，努力在烧焦密封剂和陈汗的臭味下回忆确切的字眼。过一阵，你开始比怀疑别人的贪婪更怀疑自己的记忆。

今晚，凯德正跟几个船坞老板就着埃尔德啤酒罐大笑，米拉在工具柜里重新缠缆绳，抱怨我们那套拼凑的装备是个死亡陷阱。我坐在一根货舱撑杆上，听着飞船吱嘎，琢磨哪个会先要了我们的命：一处失败的焊缝、一个错误的决定，还是有人认定少一份分成能让自己的日子好过些。

打捞王冠工会在账簿健康时叫我们一家人。家人的问题在于，当要让人消失进残骸里时，他们确切知道该往哪里下刀。
